messages:
alex: Quick note from the onboarding workshop just now — reproducible issue with JS SDK streaming + function-calls when auth refresh triggers a retry. Occasionally yields `Unexpected end of JSON input` in the schema validator.

maria: Oof. Is there a short repro we can point folks at?

alex: Yes. Steps: clone sample-app, npm i, npm run dev, visit /demo which calls `create_order` as a function with a strict JSON schema. If the access token expires mid-response and SDK performs automatic retry, the stream fragments get interleaved and the validator receives a truncated JSON chunk. Only seen in JS SDK so far.

jon: Does Python SDK do anything differently?

alex: Python accumulates the full message before schema validation, so it doesn't hit the parse error. Our JS streaming path validates as tokens arrive which is faster but fragile when retries replay interleaving fragments.

sam: Can you paste a snippet from staging logs?

alex: Pasted from staging: 

```
WARN auth: refresh token for user=alice id=23
INFO proxy: retrying request id=abcd-1234 (retry 1)
STREAM CHUNK: {"name":"create_order","args":{"items":[{"sku":"ABC","qty":1}],"shipping":{
STREAM CHUNK: "address":"123 main st","city":"Sno",)
ERROR schema-validator: Unexpected end of JSON input at parseChunk (schema.js:214)
```

maria: Looks like the retry injection replays a separate stream window and we end up with mismatched braces.

jon: We have an optimization in JS to early-validate on partial tokens to provide faster feedback. That assumption breaks if chunk boundaries can split JSON tokens, and retries make that likely.

sam: Short-term workshop workaround: set RW_SDK_STREAMING=false or RW_SDK_RETRY=0 in env so the demo doesn't hit this. Not ideal but low friction for attendees.

alex: I pushed a tiny sample-app PR that adds simple buffering in the client to reassemble top-level JSON before invoking the validator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/999

jon: We should add the same buffering into the JS SDK as an opt-in flag like `streamingStrictJson: boolean` default true. When false, buffer until a matching top-level closing brace then validate. That would match Python behavior and keep the early-validate optimization available.

maria: Please open an SDK parity issue and include an e2e that simulates a mid-stream auth refresh so we don't regress.

sam: Filed issue #1601: "JS SDK: streaming JSON + retries can produce partial-parse errors" and attached a tiny harness that simulates chunked streams + retry.

alex: I'll add a short callout in the quickstart: if you hit `Unexpected end of JSON input` during function-calls, try disabling streaming or retries while we roll a proper SDK patch.

ci-bot: deploy job started for pr/999 -> staging (job id: deploy-8101) - https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/jobs/8101

maria: Can the patch include diagnostic fields when partial-parse happens? e.g. `partial_json_len`, `last_byte_hex`, `retry_inflight=true` so SRE can triage production occurrences.

jon: Good idea. I'll add diagnostics and unit tests for partial-chunk parse + buffer reconciliation.

sam: After the SDK change merges, update the onboarding workshop script and the quickstart note to avoid surprising new users. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks folks. I'll follow up in the workshop channel and confirm staging once CI finishes.

ci-bot: deploy job deploy-8101: SUCCESS on staging - https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/jobs/8101/logs

sam: Verified staging. Buffering fix prevents the Unexpected end of JSON input in the live demo.

maria: Great. Add to release notes: "improve JSON streaming + retry robustness (JS SDK)" and include the issue link.

alex: On it. :rocket:
